sets.name: Ransomware blast radius
sets.description: Not 'is it exploitable' but 'how far does encryption spread and what does containment cost'. Five questions, one request. Read alongside the baseline set: the routing answer often survives, the blast radius does not.

containment_action.instructions: Choose the containment move for ransomware exposure on this asset, weighing how much of the estate the asset can reach. Containment is about distance, not patch difficulty.

criteria.isolate-now: The asset is internet-exposed or tier-0/tier-1: an intrusion here is one hop from systems that would stop the business. Pull it from the network before patching.
criteria.monitor-close: Reachable but low blast radius: tier-2 or below, no payments or PII classification. Tighten monitoring and egress rules rather than isolating.
criteria.patch-window: Internal-only asset where the normal patch cadence is sufficient containment; no special isolation is warranted.
criteria.needs-intel: The state does not say what this asset can reach, so containment cannot be judged. Ask the asset owner for segment and dependency data.

encryption_blast_radius.instructions: If this asset is encrypted by ransomware, how much of the estate is dragged down with it? Score the reachability, not the vulnerability itself.

criteria.name: contained
criteria.description: Loss of this asset alone is an incident nobody outside the team notices; tier-3 or lower with no shared dependencies.

criteria.name: department
criteria.description: One business function stops: an internal service such as a wiki, CI runner or report generator.

criteria.name: site
criteria.description: A whole site or product line degrades: tier-1, or a service that many teams depend on.

criteria.name: estate-wide
criteria.description: Company-wide outage or extortion leverage: internet-exposed tier-0 holding payments or regulated data.

dwell_time_suspected.instructions: Given only the CVE text and exposure in the state, how long could an attacker plausibly have been present before detection? Pre-authentication remote code execution on an exposed endpoint implies a longer window than a use-after-free behind an admin network.

criteria.name: none
criteria.description: No credible path in: unauthenticated access is impossible from the state given.

criteria.name: hours
criteria.description: Reachable, but exploitation would be noisy and short-lived before detection.

criteria.name: days
criteria.description: A quiet foothold is plausible: reachable service with no signal that anyone looked.

criteria.name: weeks
criteria.description: Pre-auth remote code execution on an internet-exposed asset with active exploitation reported.

backup_restorable.instructions: Answer yes only if the state supports a realistic restore-without-paying path. The state carries no backup evidence for any asset, so for a payments-classified tier-0 system the honest answer is no; for a low-tier internal tool with no data classification value, yes is defensible.

extortion_leverage.instructions: Answer yes if data stolen from this asset would be worth money or publicity to an attacker: payments or PII classification, or a tier-0 business-critical role.

sets.name: Backup posture
sets.description: Three questions about recovery rather than intrusion. Useful to compare against ransomware-blast-radius on the same CVE: the two sets disagree on purpose, not on facts.

restore_confidence.instructions: How confident can we be that this asset can be rebuilt from clean copies, judged only from what the state reveals about its role and data?

criteria.name: none
criteria.description: No indication of a tested restore path for stateful systems holding payments or PII.

criteria.name: unverified
criteria.description: Backups are likely to exist because the asset is managed, but nothing in the state says they were restored.

criteria.name: partial
criteria.description: Rebuildable service with mostly reproducible state: a gateway, proxy or runner that can be redeployed.

criteria.name: proven
criteria.description: Stateless or trivially reproducible internal tool where loss is an inconvenience.

backup_action.instructions: Pick the follow-up the backup answer implies.

criteria.accept: Recovery is not a concern for this asset; leave it on the normal schedule.
criteria.verify-backups: Recovery matters and is unproven: schedule a restore test as a tracked task, not an emergency.
criteria.isolate-and-verify: High-value data with an unproven restore path: treat recovery as an open risk while containment proceeds.
criteria.needs-intel: The state says too little about this asset's persistence to choose; ask the owner what state it holds.

air_gap_unknown.instructions: Answer yes when the state gives no evidence about backup isolation, which is the normal case for a scanner export and a genuine reason to escalate rather than assume safety.
